findings.body: [Testing] The new exception-log profile is absent from metadata collection: `.github/scripts/instrumentations.sh:127` registers only the default InfluxDB task, and this execution sets no `metadataConfig` label. Register `influxdb-2.4:javaagent:testExceptionSignalLogs` and label its non-default setting, for example with `telemetryConfig("otel.semconv.exception.signal.preview", "logs")`. Otherwise the generated catalog omits this profile; registering it without the label would merge its telemetry into the default profile. One representative suite is sufficient.

[Javaagent] Pre-response cancellation is reported as a failure for chunked overloads without a failure consumer, such as `query(query, 1, onNext)`. In clients 2.14 and 2.25, the internal `onFailure` throws `InfluxDBException(t)` when that consumer is absent. That library-generated exception becomes `callbackError` here, producing an ERROR span and an error-tagged duration metric for intentional cancellation. Discard this cancellation wrapper while preserving exceptions captured by the user-callback wrappers. Add a pre-response cancellation regression without a failure consumer.

[Javaagent] A non-chunked success consumer can call `dispatcher.cancelAll()` and then throw. This guard discards the user exception, and `endResponse()` also discards the thrown error because the call is canceled. The span and duration metric consequently report success. Retain exceptions from wrapped user callbacks regardless of cancellation; filter cancellation-generated transport/read failures separately. Add a cancel-then-throw regression.

Splits the InfluxDB changes from #20685, correcting query outcomes and duration timing without changing other integrations.

- **Error classification:** Classify HTTP-200 top-level and per-statement errors with bounded `error.type`, never raw error text. Retain available HTTP error codes.
- **Terminal completion:** End asynchronous and chunked operations exactly once after callbacks and chunk processing finish, retaining callback, transport, and decoding failures, including newer-client decoding failures without a failure consumer.
- **Cancellation and compatibility:** Make the call available before failure consumers run so pre-response cancellation remains successful. Preserve `DONE` handling, callback parent context, and supported 2.4 APIs.
- **Regression coverage:** Cover synchronous response errors, one asynchronous statement error, successful and failed chunked completion, one cancellation control, and a single 2.4 statement-error case, with span and duration-metric assertions. Retain HTTP `400` assertions in the existing failing-query integration test.
metadata.title: Fix InfluxDB query error classification and async completion
